problem: Brain tissue keeps dying during and after a stroke; rapid selective brain cooling could limit the damage.
business_model: Medical device sold to hospitals (pre-commercial at founding)

founders.name: Justin Olshavsky
founders.background_notes: The YC page describes him as founder of Voyage Bio and founding partner of Pioneer Bio+Health Fund.

founders.name: Robert Schultz
founders.background_notes: Described on the YC page as an MD and heart surgery resident.

founders.name: Bridget Vaughan
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no role or background given.

technical_complexity.rationale: A catheter or device that cools the brain selectively during stroke needs hardware engineering, animal and human testing and FDA clearance, hard for a three-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Device regulatory pathways and clinical evidence create barriers, but the sources found do not describe patents or clearances.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Penumbra, a thrombectomy device maker, acquired Voyage Biomedical per the YC page; date and terms not public in sources found.

market_need_then: Stroke thrombectomy was growing as a procedure and brain cooling was an open clinical question; dated 2019 sources on demand were not found.

branding.domain_note: voyage.bio now shows a generic parked page with 'This domain may be for sale'.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, interviews or brand assets were found, and the name is confusable with Voyager Biomedical, an unrelated company, in search results; for a device company sold to hospitals brand matters little.

outcome_analysis: Voyage Biomedical was a tiny medical device team working on brain cooling during stroke and was acquired by Penumbra, a stroke thrombectomy company, as the YC page states. No deal date, price or funding history was found, so it is unclear whether this was a technology purchase or an acquihire. Penumbra itself agreed to be bought by Boston Scientific in January 2026.
notes: Only the YC page and a directory (Altss) state the Penumbra acquisition; two searches found no press release, 10-K mention, date or price. An aggregator lists a US$150K pre-seed in April 2019, unverified and not recorded as a round. voyage.bio is parked. Competitors named in search results (Hybernia Medical, ThermopeutiX, BrainCool, ZOLL) came from undated or recent sources, so the list is empty. The Boston Scientific note about Penumbra comes from search result summaries (January 15, 2026).
